description: A note-block sequencer of twelve blocks in three rows, playing one, two or three tracks out of a single polyphonic pair of jacks

params.text: One beat of the sequence, holding up to four notes in one of nine subdivisions; left click to step forward, shift and left click to step back, right click to choose from a list
Sets the pitch of one note in the block: click for a keyboard carrying Rest, Tie and an Auto Advance button, or drag up and down to set the voltage
Sets how many note blocks of each track are played before the sequence returns to the first
Steps through the track layouts: A B C gives each row a track, A A B joins rows one and two and plays row three twice a cycle, A A A makes one track of all three, Chord plays columns as chords

inputs.text: Advances the sequence one note block; a polyphonic cable clocks each track from its own channel
Returns the sequence to its first note block when the voltage rises past 2V; a polyphonic cable resets each track from its own channel

outputs.text: The pitch of the note now playing, one polyphonic channel per configured track
High while a note is playing, for the length set on the menu, one polyphonic channel per configured track
A gate at the end of each cycle, one polyphonic channel per configured track

notes: nothing happens until a clock is patched; the module has no clock of its own
this build has twelve note blocks, four per row; the maker's manual says sixteen
the small button above each note block is a lock, and it carries no note of its own because it is drawn inside the block rather than as a control of the module
right-clicking a block, or dragging across several and right-clicking, opens a bulk edit menu for copying, pasting, randomising and shifting only those blocks
menu: Gate Length — sets how much of each note the gate output stays high for
Swing — delays every second note block
Clock Mode: Gate, Phase — reads the clock input either as a square wave, high above 2V and low below 0.1V, or as a ramp that advances a block when it falls from above 9V to below 1V
Chord Mode — forces every row to the same subdivisions and plays each column as a chord
Randomize — randomises the pitches or the rhythm of the whole sequence
Shift & Shuffle — shifts and shuffles the sequence from the menu, the way the Shift & Shuffle expander does from its jacks
Set Rhythm — sets every note block to one subdivision
Note Pool — sets the pool of notes the randomisers draw from, from a scale, from a keyboard, or by shifting the current pool in semitones
Copy/Paste — copies and pastes the sequence or the note pool in a portable format that other JP sequencers read
Expanders — places an expander module beside this one
